title: Fate of EXDATEs and Overrides When a Whole-Series Edit Changes the Recurrence Set
question: When a whole-series edit (recurrence_id=None) changes DTSTART, RRULE, or RDATE so that existing EXDATE values or override RECURRENCE-IDs no longer name instances of the series, are those exceptions pruned or moved along with the series?
spec_gap: RFC 5546 only says that on an entire rescheduling any instance-specific information is lost unless explicitly included in the update. No RFC defines moving EXDATE or RECURRENCE-ID values when the series start changes; RFC 5545 fixes RECURRENCE-ID to the original instance time for a given UID and SEQUENCE. The only defined shift is RANGE=THISANDFUTURE, which explicitly does not affect instances defined in separate components.

citations.verbatim_quote: Note that since this is an entire rescheduling of the event, any instance-specific information will be lost, unless explicitly included with the update "REQUEST".
For a given pair of "UID" and "SEQUENCE" property values, the "RECURRENCE-ID" value for a recurrence instance is fixed.
Subsequent instances defined in separate components are not impacted by the given recurrence instance.

options.summary: After the edit, EXDATE values and standalone overrides whose value is not a candidate instance of the updated series (DTSTART + RRULE + RDATE, before EXDATE subtraction) are removed; those that are still candidates are kept unchanged.
consequences: Simple and never leaves orphaned exceptions.
Changing only the time of day invalidates every exception: instances the user deleted reappear at the new time, and all per-instance edits are lost.

options.summary: When the edit moves DTSTART by a fixed offset without otherwise changing the pattern, EXDATE values and override RECURRENCE-IDs (and the overrides' DTSTART/DTEND) are moved by the same offset; exceptions that still cannot be mapped to a candidate instance are pruned.
consequences: Preserves the user's deletions and per-instance edits across a simple time change.
Requires defining when an edit counts as a uniform shift (for example, DST-aware wall-clock offset vs absolute duration) and what happens when RRULE also changes.
Rewrites RECURRENCE-ID values, which RFC 5545 fixes per (UID, SEQUENCE); the SEQUENCE increment on the series edit is what makes this permissible.

open_questions: Should a DATE <-> DATE-TIME transition of the series be treated as a shift (mapping each date to the new time of day) or always prune?
